newsitem.title: JAPAN: Court grants bail to ex-trader Hamanaka--Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Court grants bail to ex-trader Hamanaka--Kyodo.

text.p: A Japanese court on Monday approved the release of former star copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka on bail of 50 million yen ($409,000), Kyodo news agency reported.
A Tokyo District Court spokesman said he was unable to confirm the report, adding that all information about bail is confidential in the Japanese legal system.
Hamanaka, 49, has pleaded guilty to fraud and forgery in connection with unauthorised trades over a decade that cost his former employer, Sumitomo Corp, $2.6 billion.
The plea came at the opening of his trial on February 17. The hearings continue on March 10 with the defence planning to introduce evidence showing mitigating circumstances for his actions.
Hamanaka had asked for bail when he was arrested in October, but the request was refused at that time and he has remained in custody ever since.
Kyodo did not give any reason for the granting of bail now or why it would come in the middle of a criminal trial.

But Justice Ministry sources told Reuters that since Hamanaka had acknowledged his guilt the court likely concluded there was no reason to believe he would either try to destroy evidence or attempt to flee Japan to avoid serving a prison term.
The two counts carry a penalty of up to 15 years in prison.
Hamanaka's trading activities, which earned him the name "Mr Five Percent" for the control he wielded, are also under investigation by regulators in both Britain and the United States.
Japanese prosecutors say they have given the regulators copies of the questions they have asked Hamanaka.
However, Japan contends that since the trades took place overseas, they are not involved in trying to determine if Hamanaka or Sumitomo had tried to manipulate the world copper market. ($1=122 yen)
